opportunity: A printf/scanf call states the types of its variadic arguments in its format string, but reading it cost a second decompile of every caller: Ghidra's FormatStringAnalyzer is DecompilerDependent, so the format pointer is only visible as an input varnode of a lifted CALL. decompile-all measured +77.5% (cronie crontab), +55.1% (gnutls psktool), +43.7% (gzip), which held the option to a per-run opt-in and out of the aggressive preset, even though the recovery was real (decbench C type_match perfects 80 -> 88 of 1,133). The constant is in the image, and so is the call site.
test_name: tests/stages/kuna-formatstring-static.xml (15 assertions, 14 passes; passes 7-14 require default == off on macho_imports_arm64, fmtabi_armhf and fmtedge_x86_64; the first six: over fmt_x86_64 off = the bug, default = the fix, full = the same answer with no Listing; over fmtjoin_x86_64 off/default/full must agree on a format chosen on a jump table and on a call in an alloca frame, the two shapes the post-drive audit withdraws) + tests/cli/printf-varargs-render-untyped.json + 10 unit tests (C99 conversion matrix, length-modifier matrix, `*` widths, the long-double decline, the format-function predicate over 21 accepted / 12 refused names, the fold's arithmetic incl. PIECE at the low input's width and shifts of 64 or more, and a cmov destination the fold must not know)
inspiration: Ghidra FormatStringAnalyzer (Variadic Function Signature Override, default-off); angr _get_format_string_arg_types / _apply_format_string_type_constraints (engine_ail.py: the literal is read from the loader, not from the decompiled body)
on_alias: `on` is accepted as a spelling of `full` (what it meant while the option was on|off)

cli.off: printf("%d %s\n",(unsigned long)a0,*a1);  /* unsigned long main(unsigned int a0,unsigned long *a1) */
cli.static: printf("%d %s\n",a0,(char *)*a1);        /* unsigned long main(int a0,unsigned long *a1) */

recovered_argument.off: error(a6,v1,"%s: %s",a5);            /* the second %s argument is missing */
recovered_argument.static: error(a6,v1,"%s: %s",a5,v2);         /* and a5 is recovered as char * */

jump_table_join.unaudited_static: void sub_11b0(unsigned int a0,long a1) ... __printf_chk(1,v1,a1);   /* reviewer's gcc -O2 build of the same source, round-1 tip: the window read the default path's "default %ld\n", and a2 and the %s argument were lost while the caller still passes three */
jump_table_join.static: void report(unsigned int a0,unsigned long a1,unsigned long a2) ... __printf_chk(1,v1,a1,a2);   /* == off; KUNA_FMTSTATIC_DEBUG: fmtaudit: withdrew 0x1236 (args 3 vs declared 3, format differs) */
jump_table_join.in_the_corpus: tar O2 __fprintf_chk @0x23875: a body at 0x23a38 the Listing never decoded loads msgid 0x650fb and jumps to 0x2385a inside the window; the drive renders dcgettext(NULL,v6,5) and the site is withdrawn

alloca_frame.static: error(0,v4,v6,v8);   /* == off; fmtaudit: withdrew 0x6c24 (args 5 vs declared 4, format agrees) */

coverage.method: image ground truth = objdump, every direct call/jmp whose target is the PLT stub of a format callee the resolver accepts; seen/resolved/unresolved = KUNA_FMTSTATIC_DEBUG=1 kuna decompile-all <bin> --option formatstring full; withdrawn = fmtaudit lines; loop-only = what the second decompile found on top (re-measured on the round-2 tree)
coverage.columns: in the image (call+jmp) / seen by the pass / of which tail jumps / resolved at load / unresolved / withdrawn by the post-drive audit / resolved only by the decompile-time loop
coverage.reading: 420 of the 520 sites the Listing hands the pass resolve (81%); 420 of the 605 direct sites in the image (69%). The 85-site gap between the two denominators is the Listing's own walk coverage, not this pass: on x86-64 the recursive descent is not seeded with the committed entry inventory (that seeding is under the funcstart_patterns gate), so a function only a load-time entry oracle found contributes no edges. gzip is the pure case -- `kuna xrefs --to 0x3520` reports all six __snprintf_chk call sites and Listing::refs_to(0x3520) reports none, so gzip is byte-identical on all three values.

sweep.surface: kuna decompile-all, formatstring off vs static, every changed function classified (round 2: re-run on the tree rebased onto d3617d64, both arms from the same build)
sweep.binaries: coreutils fmt (O0, O2), coreutils ls (O2), coreutils sort (O2), grep (O0, O2), gzip (O2), diffutils diff (O2), findutils find (O2), tar (O2)
sweep.classification_note: `format-call-site` is the point; `retype-cast` is a cast dropped or added because an argument is now correctly typed; `declaration-block` and `variable-renumber` are the numbering churn a type change causes (kuna names locals in declaration order); the `other` bucket was read in full -- 89 statements whose type changed (a `%d` argument typed int makes getopt's sentinel print as -1 rather than 0xffffffff), 48 callees retyped because they forward a vararg to a format call (coreutils fmt sub_69f3 gains three `char *` parameters), and 83 add/remove hunks that are difflib alignment artifacts of the renumbering (verified: `v14 = 1;` becomes `v13 = 1; v14 = NULL;`, the two halves of one shift). gzip is byte-identical: its only format-family import is __snprintf_chk and the Listing gives the pass no edge to it.
sweep.round2_note: The 228 functions that change are a strict subset of the 230 classified in round 1 (diff sub_84f0 and tar argp_parse no longer change: the cmov fix and the audit return them to off), so every hunk lies in a function whose `other` bucket was read in full then; the round-1 subclass counts (89 statement-retyped, 83 statement-added-or-removed, 48 callee-signature-retype) describe that reading.

benchmark.corpus: decbench full_run_address_2026-09-11, 444 slices / 10,748 scored functions, DECBENCH_NO_CACHE=1
benchmark.arms: base = the shipped default (static); test = --option formatstring off
benchmark.worse_rows_read: coreutils::O2::tr and coreutils::O2-noinline::tr, make_printable_str (0.5 -> 0.375) -- the same two rows as the previous measurement, unchanged. The only C change in that function is `(unsigned long)v1` -> `(unsigned int)v1` on a %03o argument, which is correct; the score moves because the value that was spilled to stack -0x58 is now a register-only variable, and decbench scores variables[] (args + stack symbols), which never carries a register local. The emitted C is equal or better.

full_vs_static.worse_rows: grep::O2::Pcompile and grep::O2-noinline::Pcompile (0.235 -> 0.176), the same pair as before
full_vs_static.reading: the second decompile buys a small aggregate gain and no new perfect function, for the +13% wall time on a printf-heavy binary -- which is the whole case for `static` being the default and `full` staying opt-in. The two worse rows are the read-only propagation `full` turns on around the drive, not the format typing.

speed.method: interleaved `kuna decompile-all` wall time (off / static / full in one round) on the round-2 build, box shared with other lanes' workspace suites; min-of-N plus the paired median of per-round deltas
speed.pass_itself: +31 ms paired median over 9 interleaved rounds (round 1), isolated by decompiling ONE function out of bash so the whole load (Listing build included) is measured against a decompile that is not; round 2 adds no load-time work
speed.note: ls's first run read +7.59% on the min with a -2.56% paired median: its off arm drew one quiet 13.9 s round in rounds ranging 13.9-23.3 s. Re-run alone at a quieter moment it reads +2.89% min / +0.02% paired median. The audit adds a walk over the call specs of a function that has a parked site, and a second drive only where it withdraws one (0 of the functions in fmt/ls/sort). `full`'s +15% on ls is the second decompile, and is why it is not the default.

preset_decision: `formatstring` leaves the AGGRESSIVE_OVERRIDES exclusion list. It was excluded for the second decompile's cost; `static` does not pay it, and it needs the Listing, which the preset supplies.
notes: Three defects were found and fixed while measuring, all of them pre-existing in the loop and all of them newly visible because the feature became the default: the override's positional parameter names leaked into the CALLER's locals (coreutils fmt rendered two different values as `error(0,*v2,"%s: %s",param3,param3)` with one of them undeclared); `%c` lowered to a plain byte rather than the char family, so a %c argument stopped printing as a character literal; and a `long double` conversion lowered to an 8-byte float, which is the wrong x86-64 SysV argument CLASS and grew two phantom parameters on coreutils numfmt simple_strtod_human. Review round 2 found two shapes where the load-time answer is wrong for the drive -- a jump-table join the Listing cannot see, and an alloca frame whose pushed return-address slot a closed prototype takes as one more argument -- and the fix is a post-drive audit (decompile_step.rs audit_parked_format_sites) that withdraws a contradicted override and drives once more. Running it over 129 binaries exposed a third, in the fold: a cmovcc destination was set unconditionally. The fold's PIECE is now concatenated at the low input's width, and shifts of 64 or more fold to zero.
